tool.name: FAIRe to Darwin Core
tool.description: presence and absence records for GBIF and OBIS
tool.command: python '$__tool_directory__/faire2dwc.py' '$workbook' --workbook_name '$workbook.element_identifier' #if str($assays).strip(): --assays '$assays' #end if $absences #if $taxa: --taxa '$taxa' #end if --country_code '$country_code' --target '$target' --title '$eml.title' --abstract '$eml.abstract' --keywords '$eml.keywords' #if str($eml.licence) != 'workbook': --licence '$eml.licence' #end if --given_name '$eml.given_name' --surname '$eml.surname' --organisation '$eml.organisation' --email '$eml.email' --orcid '$eml.orcid' --archive '$archive' --occurrence '$occurrence' --dna '$dna' --eml '$eml_xml' --report '$report'

param.name: workbook
param.label: FAIRe workbook
param.help: Checked with FAIRe-fier. For targeted assays: sampleMetadata with detected_notDetected (one column per assay), and ampData if you have it. For metabarcoding: otuFinal and taxaFinal sheets.

param.name: assays
param.label: Assays to publish (optional)
param.help: Assay names as in assay_name, separated by commas. Leave empty for all.

validator.message: Use letters, digits, spaces and _ . + ( ) , - only

param.name: absences
param.label: Write absences (targeted assays)
param.help: A record with occurrenceStatus absent for each sample where the target was not detected. GBIF's guide encourages absences for targeted detection. Metabarcoding records are always presences.

param.name: taxa
param.label: Taxon table (optional)
param.help: A column called name, with each name as the workbook gives it (targetTaxonomicAssay, or the name in taxaFinal), and any of scientificName, scientificNameID, taxonRank, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family and genus. OBIS needs scientificNameID, a WoRMS LSID such as urn:lsid:marinespecies.org:taxname:107381.

param.name: country_code
param.label: Country code (optional)
param.help: ISO 3166-1 two-letter code, such as AU. Needed only when the country in geo_loc_name is not one the tool knows (the report says).

has_text.text: target DNA amplified in 2 of 3 technical replicates (mean Cq 33.55)
CmaeCOI: 1 present, 2 absent, 1 sample not written
CmaeND2: 2 present, 2 absent, 1 detection taken from ampData
scientificNameID is empty in 2 of 2 records
kingdom is empty in 2 of 2 records
MiFish: 3 present, 1 detection with no taxon name, 1 control column
creator and contact from project_contact: given name Casey, surname Sampler, casey.sampler@example.org
assay NotAnAssay is not in projectMetadata

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool turns a FAIR eDNA (`FAIRe <https://fair-edna.github.io/>`_) workbook into a Darwin Core archive that you can publish through an IPT (Integrated Publishing Toolkit) to GBIF or OBIS. It is for **presence and absence** data:
- **Targeted assays** (qPCR, ddPCR): one record per sample and assay, *present* where detected_notDetected is 1 and *absent* where it is 0. GBIF's `guide to publishing DNA-derived data <https://doi.org/10.35035/doc-vf1a-nr22>`_ calls this targeted species detection, and has no Metabarcoding Data Toolkit route for it. - **Metabarcoding data reported as presence**: one record per sample and sequence with reads (or a 1) in otuFinal, named from taxaFinal. Read counts are not published. For read counts, use **FAIRe2MDT** or **edna2obis**.
Controls (samp_category other than *sample*) are always left out.
-----
**Inputs**
- **FAIRe workbook**, ideally one that FAIRe-fier accepts.
- Targeted: sampleMetadata with detected_notDetected (detected_notDetected_<assay> for each assay when there are several), and targetTaxonomicAssay for each assay in projectMetadata, which gives the name of each record. ampData, when filled, adds the number of technical replicates that amplified, the mean Cq and the mean copy number. A sample with no detected_notDetected value but with ampData rows counts as detected when at least one replicate amplified, and the report says how many. A sample whose value is a missing-value term (*missing: not provided*) is not written. - Metabarcoding: otuFinal and taxaFinal (otuFinal_<assay> and taxaFinal_<assay> for several assays). otuFinal columns are samp_name or lib_id. Sequences with no taxon name are left out.
- **Taxon table** (optional): names to publish and their identifiers and higher taxonomy, one row per name as the workbook gives it. OBIS needs a WoRMS LSID (scientificNameID) for every name; GBIF matches names to its backbone itself, but kingdom is highly recommended. - **Dataset details**: the title, abstract, creator and licence for the EML. With no name or organisation given, the creator and contact come from project_contact and institution in projectMetadata. You can also add or change these later in the IPT. GBIF takes CC0 1.0, CC BY 4.0 and CC BY-NC 4.0.
**Outputs**
- **Darwin Core archive** (zip): meta.xml, eml.xml, occurrence.txt (the core) and dna_derived_data.txt (the DNA derived data extension), ready to upload to an IPT. - **Occurrence** and **DNA derived data** tables, the same as in the archive, to look at in Galaxy. - **EML**, the dataset metadata. - **Report**: the records written for each assay, the samples and controls left out, the columns written, and what GBIF or OBIS will still want (such as coordinates, kingdom or scientificNameID).
**How FAIRe terms become Darwin Core**
The table *faire2dwc_terms.tsv*, next to the tool, lists every Darwin Core term written and the FAIRe term it comes from. A few are made by the tool:
- occurrenceID is project_id, samp_name and assay (and seq_id for metabarcoding); eventID is project_id and samp_name; basisOfRecord is MaterialSample. - country and locality come from geo_loc_name; countryCode from the country, or the form. - occurrenceRemarks says which assay detected the target, in how many technical replicates, and the detection criteria. quantificationCycle is the mean Cq of the replicates that amplified; estimatedNumberOfCopies and organismQuantity are the mean copy number of all replicates. - FAIRe's missing-value terms are written as empty cells.
-----
**Limits**
- The tool does not look names up in WoRMS or GBIF. Use the taxon table, or **edna2obis: match taxa** for metabarcoding names. - Records are published as the workbook gives them. Check the detection criteria and the controls before publishing: a positive field control, for example, may mean some detections are contamination. - The IPT checks the archive again when you upload it.
